title: OH/IR stars in the inner Galactic bulge: I. Colour, CO line, and stellar light curve characteristics
question: Obtain information on the mass loss of O-rich AGB stars, and on its transformations in geometry and kinematics that occur at the tip of the AGB.

data.sensitivity: Line rms: ~7, 4, 5 mJy/beam (B3 at 3 km/s, B6 at 2 km/s, B7 at 2 km/s); Continuum rms: ~0.06, 0.1, 0.2 mJy/beam (107, 233, 338 GHz)

what.value: Survey of OH/IR stars in the inner Galactic bulge (source catalog and OH 1612 MHz flux densities and velocities)

evidence.quote: The survey of OH/IR stars by (cite: seveetal97a) forms the basis of our sample.

what.value: ALMA 13CO(3-2) data for three objects where part of the line was missed, and median luminosity (5400 L_sun) used for sample selection

evidence.quote: We selected all objects, brighter than 0.3 Jy in the OH 1612 MHz line, that have an estimated luminosity within a factor of two of the median luminosity of the O+22 sample, 5400 $L_\odot$.
Despite this, part of the $^{13}$CO(3–2) line was missed for seven objects (for three of these objects the data of O+22 were used instead).

what.value: Distance to the Galactic centre of 8.2 kpc

evidence.quote: The adopted distance to all of our sources is 8.2 kpc (cite: gravcoll19), even though some spread along the line of sight is most likely.

what.value: Reddening E(J - Ks) towards each source

evidence.quote: The reddening $E$($J$ $-$ $K_{\rm s}$) towards each source was calculated using the results of (cite: gonzetal18)

what.value: Extinction conversion to A_Ks and extrapolation up to 8 um

evidence.quote: converted into extinction in the $K_{\rm s}$ band, $A_{K_{\rm s}}$, and extrapolated up to 8 $\mu$m using the relationships provided by (cite: nishetal09).

what.value: Extinction law in the range 8 to 30 um

evidence.quote: In the range 8 to 30 $\mu$m we use the extinction law provided by (cite: xueetal16).

recipe.goal: Determine source positions and continuum flux densities
recipe.method: Fit two-dimensional Gaussians in the image plane to the continuum images and to the moment 0 images integrated over the circumstellar line velocity range (using 12CO(3-2) for canonical positions).

recipe.goal: Characterize infrared SEDs, variability, and classify objects into four categories
recipe.method: Correct Spitzer, MSX, and WISE photometry for extinction; construct mid-IR colour-colour diagrams to separate standard (SdE) and detached (DdE) dust envelopes; fit single-period sinusoids to VVV Ks and WISE W1/W2 light curves to separate regular large-amplitude pulsators (P) from non-periodic/low-amplitude (nP); inspect 12CO moment 8 maps and line profiles to separate standard (SgE) and complex (CgE) gas envelopes.
key_parameters: Counterpart search radius: 6'' from ALMA coordinates
assumptions: Single pulsation period assumed for light curve fitting

recipe.goal: Derive and fit azimuthally averaged radial brightness profiles (AARPs) for SgE objects
recipe.method: Convolve data cubes with a circular Gaussian of FWHM equal to the major axis of the synthesised beam, average within +-20% of the gas expansion velocity around the systemic velocity in concentric circular annuli of width equal to the convolving beam, and fit a Moffat function to determine Theta_0.5 and Theta_0.1.
key_parameters: Velocity range: +-20% of gas expansion velocity centred on systemic velocity; size metric: Theta_0.1 (radius at 10% of peak)
assumptions: Distance of 8.2 kpc to the Galactic centre

recipe.goal: Extract multi-aperture CO line profiles and fit line shapes, intensities, and kinematics
recipe.method: Convolve data cubes to circular Gaussian beams of FWHM 0.5'', 1'', 2'', and 3'' (or down to 0.2'' when affected by ISM contamination), extract spectra from the central source pixel, and fit the CLASS/GILDAS 'Shell' profile (or parabola for C18O) for SgE objects and Gaussian profiles (with visual kinematics) for CgE objects.
key_parameters: Convolved beam FWHMs: 0.5'', 1'', 2'', 3'' (and 0.2'' for contaminated cases); C18O extracted from 2'' data
assumptions: SgE objects have spherical CSEs formed by constant MLR expanding at constant velocity

recipe.goal: Reduce APEX single-dish spectra and compare with ALMA 3'' fluxes to estimate interferometric flux loss
recipe.method: Subtract first-order polynomial baseline from APEX spectra, average polarisations, convert T_A* to Jy, bin to 2 km s^-1, and compute ALMA(3'')/APEX velocity-integrated line intensity ratios after excluding sources with CSM/ISM interaction contamination.
key_parameters: Conversion factors: 35, 36, and 46 Jy K^-1 at 230, 345, and 461 GHz; velocity resolution: 2 km s^-1

evidence.quote: The gas expansion velocities from our line fits form a relatively narrow distribution, from 5 to 24 km s$^{-1}$, Fig. [7](#f:kinematics_abcd). The average and standard deviation are 15 $\pm$ 4 km s$^{-1}$.
When detections are made in more than one band, the flux densities result in an average spectral index $\alpha$ ($S_\nu$ $\propto$ $\nu^\alpha$) of 3.5 $\pm$ 0.6 (ten objects).
As for SgE objects, the relative occurrence rates in the three bands are fully explained by a steep spectral index (3.3 $\pm$ 0.3, seven objects).

score_reason: ALMA project code, CASA pipeline version, calibrators, spectral setup, weighting, velocity binning, convolved beam sizes (0.5''-3''), and analytical fitting formulae (Moffat and Shell profiles) are all explicitly specified, with only standard tclean imaging parameters (cell size, stopping threshold, masking) left unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Single public ALMA project (2023.1.00098.S) with a clear, well-specified observational recipe (pipeline calibration, robust=0.5 imaging, Gaussian beam convolution to 0.5''-3'', Moffat AARP fitting, and CLASS Shell profile fitting) yielding well-defined statistical and per-source numeric metrics.
